intro: A service can allow short bursts while bounding sustained traffic. A token bucket refills over elapsed time, caps stored credit, and charges only admitted requests.
task: Simulate burst admission over time, capping refills and preserving credit after rejected requests.
requirements: times and costs are equal-length nonempty finite vectors. times must be nonnegative and nondecreasing; costs must be nonnegative. capacity and refill_rate are nonnegative finite scalars.
Start with a full bucket at time 0. Before each request add elapsed_time*refill_rate, capped at capacity. Accept when cost<=available tokens, including equality.
Subtract cost only on acceptance. Return dict allowed as a boolean vector and remaining as token balances immediately after each request. Equal timestamps receive no refill.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Update time even after rejection
hints.body: Elapsed time is measured since the previous request, regardless of admission.

hints.title: Cap before charging
hints.body: Refill first, clamp to capacity, then decide whether the request can spend its cost.

explanation: The capacity controls the maximum burst while refill rate controls replenishment over time. A long idle period cannot build unlimited credit because the balance is capped.
This simulation is deterministic and single-threaded. A real shared limiter needs atomic state updates and a defined clock policy to preserve the same admission semantics under concurrency.
